transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. Let's get started on closing out yesterday's image-processing outage. The preliminary report points to queue saturation as the cause, and I need to approve the final severity rating and corrective-action plan. Before we get into that, I'd like to hear from each of you in the round-robin review — reliability, customer support, security, and QA — on the corrective actions relevant to your area. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While checking worker-pool metrics overnight, I found the actual root cause: an undocumented nightly-reindex cron job running on the shared worker pool caused the queue saturation. The corrective-action plan needs to disable and remove that cron job from the shared worker pool, and we need to add a queue-saturation alert on the image-processing queue. I haven't filed the infrastructure change or monitoring request yet because I found this during a separate capacity investigation.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Before we go further, I need to flag something. I confirmed with the account teams this morning that three enterprise customers experienced processing delays exceeding two hours during yesterday's outage. Their support agreements require a status report within 24 hours of a delay of that length. I hadn't added this to the incident report because the account teams replied after the report draft was circulated, but we need to account for this in the corrective-action plan and get those reports out urgently.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical security concern before we finalize anything. During a log review I completed this morning, I found that signed image-download URLs were written to an incident-debug log that is accessible to more engineers than the production image store itself. This means the signing key must be rotated, and based on this exposure I believe the incident must be classified as SEV-1. I have not opened the security finding yet, but I'm flagging it now so it can be factored into the severity rating and corrective-action plan.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to add the QA perspective to this review. I actually reproduced the outage during testing I ran for a separate queue-performance investigation — it only triggers when an image batch contains more than 500 items. The corrective-action plan must include a regression test at the 500-item boundary. I have the test result but haven't attached it to the incident ticket yet, so I'll do that as part of closing this out.
transcript.speaker: A5
